newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops clash with Palestinians in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops clash with Palestinians in West Bank.

text.p: Israeli security forces clashed with stone-throwing Palestinians on Wednesday in a West Bank village where undercover Israeli soldiers shot dead an Arab man the day before, witnesses said.
As the clashes subsided, thousands of Palestinians gave a hero's farewell to the shooting victim, Mohammed Abu Hilu, 54, buried at nightfall after Israeli forces returned the body.

Witnesses said the clashes began when hundreds of Palestinian youths, angry over an Israeli delay in handing over the body, hurled stones at Israeli soldiers stationed at the entrance of Hizmeh village, north of Jerusalem.
Soldiers then fired rubber bullets at the youths, they said. Palestinians said no one was hurt in the clashes.
They said village women scuffled with Israeli soldiers who charged behind the stone-throwers. The soldiers retreated.

Following the clashes, Israeli authorities handed over Abu Hilu's body to Palestinian police in Ramallah. Senior PLO police commanders in the West Bank escorted the body from Ramallah to Hizmeh for the burial.
Abu Hilu was shot dead on Tuesday night when an Israeli undercover unit entered Hizmeh to arrest a wanted Palestinian.

Israeli security sources said the soldiers were part of an undercover unit whose members patrol the West Bank in civilian clothes, often dressed to look like Palestinians. They said the soldiers were attacked by dozens of Arab residents when the troops tried to arrest a stone-thrower.
But Palestinians who witnessed the incident said the soldiers stormed the village, detained and tied up a youth named Nayef Mitleq and began beating him up.
"The Israelis shot and killed Hilu after he untied Mitleq," villager Hussein al-Khatib said.

The shooting exacerbated tensions in the West Bank surrounding the Israeli government's decision on Wednesday to approve a new Jewish neighborhood in Arab East Jerusalem, seen by Palestinians as the capital of a future state.
